ios.desc:
Halo is a personal AI companion that connects to the sources already on your phone (mail, calendar, reminders, health, music, and more) and helps you act on what matters. There's no backend storing your information. Your emails, memories, and context stay entirely on your device, every connection is made directly from your phone, and AI runs through API keys you control.

As you use Halo, it builds a private memory of facts about you: your identity, preferences, relationships, and routines, synthesized from your connected sources. Over time it becomes genuinely useful because it actually knows you, without that knowledge ever leaving your hands. Private by architecture, not by promise.

Features:

- A private memory that grows with you
Halo builds a wiki-style knowledge base from your connected sources. It writes notes by topic, organizes them, and links related ones together. Think of it as a second brain that stays on your device. Open Settings > Memory > Memory Graph to see how everything connects.

- Search by meaning, not just keywords
Ask "When is my next trip?" and Halo finds "Flight to Tokyo departs Friday," even though the words don't match. It passes the most relevant details to the AI before it answers, so replies are personal and grounded in your own information. That search runs entirely on your phone.

- An agent that gets things done
Halo breaks a request into steps, picks the right tools, and follows through. It can research a topic, organize information, work with files, and take action across your connected services, instead of just telling you what to do.

- Bring your own AI
Connect the AI provider you prefer using your own API key, and switch any time. You choose who processes your requests, and there's no middleman server.

- Voice & Meeting Notes
Record meetings and Halo transcribes & differentiates speakers locally, then uses the LLM you choose to summarise the transcript and generate actionable insights.

- Connect your favorite services
Use MCP connectors to link the apps and services you already use. Browser automations let Halo work with websites you're already signed in to.

- Recurring tasks
Schedule Halo to check for updates, gather information, or handle routine online tasks on a regular basis. Everything runs on your device, and you can review what happened.

- A built-in workspace for files
Halo has its own command-line environment to create, search, organize, and transform files, and to run scripts when a task calls for i

show_hn.title: Show HN: Halo – A Personal AI with On-Device Harness, Memory and Browser Agent

quotes.text:
Halo is privacy focused personal assistant for iOS that uses a custom built agent harness with support to use you existing LLM subscriptions, Wiki based memory system backed by on-device RAG, a full-fledged local browser agent, chat with generative UI and more.

TLDR: It's a better version of Hermes/OpenClaw for iOS, without needing a server! The better part is its proactive feature set and UX.

---

I started building Halo last year with 3 goals in mind: 
- Surface what’s important before I have to ask
- Understand my life through the apps I already use
- Keep my personal data on my device

Privacy is at the core of Halo and that's what sets it apart from other AI assistants. While other popular assistants on iOS save your private data such as emails, messages, etc on their servers, Halo stores all of it on your device.

I launched it today and have a 50% discount for the first week for early adopters. There is no subscription, just a single lifetime plan with a no-charge-at-end free trial. US price is $49 with PPP of up to 80% off for other countries like India.

More details here:

Official website: https://meethalo.app

Read more about the memory system: https://meethalo.app/blog/how-halo-remembers/

X posts about building it publicly: https://x.com/search?q=from%3Atanmays%20halo

---
